source_note: Topic structure follows the CCEA GCSE Religious Studies specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

topics.name: Unit 4: Introduction to the Gospel of Matthew
Unit 5: Introduction to the Gospel of Mark

connections.why: Church teaching is grounded in beliefs about how God is revealed
Claims about revelation feed into philosophical arguments for God's existence
The two synoptic gospels share material and invite comparison of their portraits of Jesus
Church teaching shapes the ethical positions Christians take
Ethical reasoning draws on philosophical questions about God and morality
The gospel accounts of Jesus underpin the beliefs and practices of the Church
Islam and Judaism share Abrahamic roots, inviting comparison of belief and practice
Islamic belief centres on revelation through the Qur'an, a contrasting model of revelation
Jewish and Christian ethics share scriptural foundations and can be compared
